summary: Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1948 to 1953. He held an academic post at Hokkaido University.
Specializing in history, archaeology, and Japanology, Hiroshi Kanaseki studied at Kyoto University from circa 1948 to 1953. He later served at Tenri University from circa 1968 to 1993.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, Hiroshi Kanno studied at the University of Tokyo. He held directorships at Soka University and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2003–2009), later becoming professor at the International University of Health and Welfare in 2015.

Hiroshi Kuroda, who worked in Indology and philosophy, completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University in circa 1976. He held assistant professor posts at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1990) and Osaka Gakuin Junior College (circa 1986–1991).

An Indologist and philosopher, Hiroshi Marui earned degrees at the University of Tokyo, studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, and studied under Albrecht Wezler. His posts included Musashino University and an assistant professorship at the University of Tokyo (1992, 1995, 1999–2018).
Hiroshi Maruyama worked in Indology. He held a professorship at Osaka University and headed the Ayurveda Research Society, both attested in 1987.
Hiroshi Nemoto, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, completed his MA at Hiroshima University. He later served there as professor, attested in 2015–2016 and 2026.
Hiroshi Tokushige works in Buddhist studies. His career includes posts at Koyasan University as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and special appointed lecturer (attested 2026).
A specialist in Indology and religious studies, Hiroshi Yamashita was an exchange student at the University of Madras. He served as associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).

Hirotaka Kato works in Buddhist studies. He was a research assistant at Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as a director at Soka University (attested 2010–2012).
A philosopher, Hiroyuki Kato held posts at Bansho Shirabesho (circa 1860–1862) and Kaisei School (circa 1863–1869), followed by a position at the University of Tokyo from circa 1877 to 1893.
Linguist Hisanosuke Izui studied at Kyoto University from circa 1925 to 1928. He later held an academic appointment at Kyoto Sangyo University from circa 1969 to 1980.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Hisao Inagaki earned degrees from Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Ryukoku University, and the University of London (PhD 1968). He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki, active in Buddhist studies, studied at Doshisha University (~1937–1941). He was a professor at Kobe University (~1962–1974), professor emeritus at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1974–1982), and professor at Komazawa University (~1982–1989).

Hisao Takahashi, working in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Taisho University and under Ryukai Mano. At Taisho University, he served as assistant (~1975–1985), lecturer (~1993–1997), and professor (~2002–2015).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Hisashi Matsumura studied under Jan Willem de Jong. He held posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and Kobe Shinwa University as assistant professor (attested 1996).

Specializing in Tibetology and history and archaeology, Hisashi Sato studied at Kyoto University (~1934–1937). He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Komazawa University (~1977–1984), and Toyo University, and held a post at Bukkyo University (~1984–1989).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Hisataka Ishida studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser. He became a full-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Philosopher Hisatake Kato studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). His academic posts included Yamagata University (~1970–1985), Tohoku University (~1985–1990), the University of Tokyo (~1999–2001), Tottori University of Environmental Studies (~2001–2007), and the University of Human Arts and Sciences (~2007–2011).
